column1: # Import libraries whose archive shape differs from what the pinned LINK
# /IMPLIB (VC6 LINK 6.00, short import members) emits. `format` names the
# pinned toolchain whose LINK produced the shape:
#   vc2  = VC 2.0 LINK 2.50: descriptor `<DLL>_IMPORT_DESCRIPTOR` and its own
#          `NULL_IMPORT_DESCRIPTOR`, so the image gets a second .idata$3
#          terminator;
#   vc41 = VC4.1 LINK 3.10: the pre-VC5 long import format, one full COFF
#          member per import, with no @comp.id (Rich prodid 0). When the vc41
#          toolchain ships `<stem>.lib` itself, that SDK library is linked
#          unchanged (NETAPI32); otherwise the library is synthesised with
#          LINK 3.10 and kept exactly as LINK writes it.
# LINK names every archive member after the DLL name it records for the
# import (docs/patterns/link310-import-member-names.md), and the image's
# linker orders each DLL's .idata$4/$5 group by that name. The stub DLL is
# linked under the retail DLL name, so its members carry exactly that name;
# homm1.graph.implib verifies it and edits no byte of the produced library.
# Buka's Rich header counts 179 short
# imports (prodid 1), 30 unmarked objects, 11 LINK 5.12.8034 objects (the VC6
# Platform SDK descriptors: five libraries x 2 + __NULL_IMPORT_DESCRIPTOR)
# and 2 LINK 6.00.8447 objects (audiere.lib's descriptor pair). Of the 200
# imports, 21 are therefore long members: WING32's 6 (WinG SDK) plus 15 from
# exactly three libraries, and with these three rows the candidate's Rich
# counts, IAT slot order and .idata$6 hints equal retail's.
dll
mss32.dll
column3: Rich: 5 long imports + 2 unmarked descriptors; with VC6 short members the mss32 IAT order reverses

column3: Rich: 9 long ordinal imports + 2 unmarked descriptors; the smackw32 IAT order matches only in the long format
